patients.summary: Healthy construction project coordinator who joins the practice at 26. In July 2025 he has Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP) treated with IVIG and recovers; a year later he has a recurrence as the Miller Fisher variant (anti-GQ1b positive) and is recovering as of today.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M here to set up primary care. Wants a practice closer to home; records release signed today.

No complaints. Feels well. No meds, no supplements. NKDA. No surgeries, no hospital stays.

FHx: father with high blood pressure, on treatment and well controlled. Mother hypothyroid. Nobody in the immediate family with autoimmune disease or nerve/muscle disorders that he knows of.

Social: works as a project coordinator for a construction firm, splits time between the office and job sites. Lives alone in South Hadley. Never smoked, no vaping. Couple of beers a week, sometimes three. No drug use.

ROS: negative across the board. Sleeps fine, mood good.

Exam: well-appearing young man, comfortable. Vitals as charted, BP normal. HEENT clear, TMs normal, oropharynx normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro: strength and gait normal, reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, healthy adult. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and HCV screening, he agrees. Tdap today, last one he can recall was in high school. Flu and COVID once the fall supply is in, will set up a nurse visit.
2. Records requested from prior PCP.

Return in a year for a physical.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Tyler,

All of your labs from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver function, blood sugar and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screening tests were both negative, and those don't need repeating unless something changes.

No action needed. We'll message you when flu shots are in.

Your primary care team

documents.title: Records from Prior Primary Care Practice
documents.author: prior primary care
documents.body:
Records summary, prior primary care office (records through spring 2023), received by fax.

Patient: Tyler Griffin, DOB 01/26/1997.

Visits: annual physicals at ages 21 through 25, all unremarkable. One sick visit at 23 for a sore throat, rapid strep negative, symptomatic care.

Problem list: none.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.

Immunizations: childhood series complete, including MMR x2, varicella x2, hepatitis B x3 and meningococcal conjugate at 11 and 16; HPV series completed in adolescence; COVID primary series 2021.

No outstanding referrals or results.

[Scanned to chart, reviewed by PCP 10/05.]

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu and COVID shots before work. Feeling well, no fever, no prior reactions to vaccines. Flu given L deltoid, COVID (2023-24 formula) given R deltoid. VIS provided for both. Waited 15 min, no problems, left for a job site.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient called, concrete pour got moved to tomorrow morning and he has to be on site. Cancelled 9/17 physical, rebooked for Tuesday 9/24 at 8:00.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 27M.

Interval: nothing new since last fall. No ER or urgent care visits. Busy season at work, lots of hours on job sites, otherwise good. Still no meds.

Habits unchanged: never smoker, a few drinks a week, no drugs. Wears hearing protection and steel toes on site. Seat belt always.

ROS negative. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP fine, weight steady from last year. Normal HEENT, neck without nodes or thyromegaly, heart regular without murmur, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no edema, skin clear, neuro grossly intact.

A/P: Well adult.
- Labs last year all normal, no repeat needed this year.
- Flu and updated COVID given.
- Testicular self-exam reviewed.
- Next physical fall 2025.
